claims.text: The dynamic mechanical response of as-solidified, equiatomic Co-free FeNiCrMn is governed by a transition between dislocation glide and deformation twinning.
Dislocation glide dominates deformation at room temperature and moderate or quasi-static strain rates.
Deformation twinning becomes increasingly active as strain rate increases.
Deformation twinning becomes increasingly active as temperature decreases.
The proposed material is equiatomic FeNiCrMn in a cast, homogenized, minimally thermomechanically processed condition.
This material condition is representative of a cost-effective Co-free configuration.
A fully crossed strain-rate and temperature test matrix can isolate the effects of those variables on deformation mechanisms.
An argon atmosphere prevents oxidation during testing.
Twin density and distribution relative to dislocation structures mediate the dynamic mechanical response.
At elevated strain rates, reduced thermal activation favors deformation-twin nucleation.
At lower temperatures, reduced thermal activation favors deformation-twin nucleation.
Deformation twins act as additional barriers to dislocation motion.
Twin density and associated strain hardening increase relative to the quasi-static room-temperature baseline as strain rate increases.
Twin density and associated strain hardening increase relative to the quasi-static room-temperature baseline as temperature decreases.
The proposed mechanism is expected to apply specifically to homogenized FeNiCrMn retaining an as-solidified material condition.
Additional work hardening or significant casting defects may alter the competition between dislocation glide and deformation twinning.
Short-range ordering may contribute to the observed dynamic response.
